label: Mark van Roojen, Moral Cognitivism vs §5.2…: Every moral sentence has the surface syntax of a…
locator: §5.2, 'Normative discourse seems to meet both of these constraints relatively straightforwardly'
interpretation: Divers and Miller (1994): moral sentences meet both minimalist constraints, surface assertoric syntax with embedding and disciplined use. The entry hedges ('seems'); the claim records the position it reports, stated for every moral sentence. That some moral sentences are true, which the entry adds as a possible consequence ('may mean'), is not formalized. Attribution reading on a secondary witness: the claim records the position the entry reports, not a thesis of the entry's author. No primary text is pinnable (in copyright, no immutable open text).
